🔔 Bitcoin price nears Fidelity’s power law support: Accumulation zone or missing catalyst? 

📌 On his power law model, a logarithmic chart that bounds Bitcoin’s entire price history between an upper resistance curve, a middle trendline, and a lower support curve, the floor currently sits near 58,000 dollars. That lower line has caught every major Bitcoin bottom since 2015. Timmer’s label for the zone the market has now entered is unambiguous: accumulation. His caveat is just as unambiguous: he sees no catalyst for a reversal, and he is not calling a bottom.

⚠️ That combination, a historically reliable floor approaching and a strategist refusing to ring the bell, is the most honest summary of the Bitcoin market in July 2026. The asset is coming off its worst quarter since the 2022 bear market, spot ETFs just recorded their largest quarterly outflow since launch, the speculative premium that carried the price past 120,000 dollars last year has evaporated, and the fast money has visibly rotated elsewhere, first into gold, then into semiconductor stocks. And yet the two quantitative measures Timmer trusts most, the deviation from the power law trendline and the Bitcoin-to-gold ratio, have both sunk to depths recorded at exactly two prior moments: the 2018 low and the 2022 low. Both of those moments were generational buying opportunities. Both also felt like the end of the world at the time.

🔖 This feature takes the model seriously in both directions: what the power law actually says, why its track record earns attention, and why the missing-catalyst objection is not a hedge but the core of the analysis.

💬 Latest US attacks target several locations across Iran, leaving two dead and 11 injured

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The latest US missile and air attacks have targeted several locations across Iran, including areas in the southern and central provinces, leaving at least two people dead and 11 others injured, according to local officials.

In the southern Khuzestan Province, two people were killed and 11 others injured early Thursday after missiles struck the area around the passenger terminal at the Shalamcheh border crossing, according to the province’s deputy governor for security and law enforcement affairs.
​
Missile attacks also targeted an area near the city of Andimeshk, as well as two locations around the cities of Ahvaz and Ramshir, Valiollah Hayati said, adding that one of the targets near Ramshir was an asphalt storage warehouse.
​
In Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari Province, an area in the Kiar County came under an air attack in the early hours of Thursday. The province’s deputy governor for political, security and social affairs, Abdolali Arzhang, said there were no casualties, adding that relevant authorities were assessing the incident and possible damage.
​
In the southern Hormuzgan Province, two maritime search-and-rescue vessels were hit in a US attack. The vessels sustained serious damage.
​
Meanwhile, agricultural equipment belonging to farmers in Dashti County, Bushehr Province, was hit by US missiles in two separate attacks, according to the province’s deputy governor for political and security affairs. Ehsan Jahanian said the county had come under missile attacks on three occasions on Thursday, with no casualties reported. The extent of the damage was still being assessed.
​
Several areas of Bushehr city were also targeted in two separate missile attacks earlier in the day, with no fatalities reported.
